Cc: ops@brightlane.com
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Odd partial gap in streaming response — example attached

Hi Tessa,

We saw an odd behavior this morning while using the streaming completion for our chat assistant. Roughly 1 in 1200 requests returned what looks like a sudden missing middle chunk — the response starts, then there is a ~2 second pause, then the stream resumes but a sentence in the middle is absent. We've attached a screenshot of the terminal output and included the request ID that the SDK printed (request_id: brl-9f3a2c).

Example: (user prompt elided)
- Expected: "...we recommend migrating the DB in two phases to avoid downtime."
- Observed: "...we recommend migrating the DB in two" [gap] "to avoid downtime."

No HTTP error status was returned; the SDK shows the stream as completed. We can repro locally 2x out of ~300 tries when running a short batch test. This is low frequency but reproducible for us.

Attachments: response-screenshot.png

Could your team take a look? We can capture a HAR if that helps.

Thanks,
Sarah Thompson
Head of Integrations
Brightlane

Hi Sarah — thanks for the report and the screenshot, this is helpful. I'm looping in Marissa from SRE and Sean from Support so we can triage quickly.

Initial notes / ask from us:
- Could you share the raw request_id(s) (you sent one: brl-9f3a2c) and the timestamp window when you saw the hit?
- If you can reproduce, please run the quick test below that forces a non-transcoded, single-connection stream and paste the raw output (so we can rule out SDK-side buffering):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"<your prompt>","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams

We will review our ingress and streamer logs for that request id. At first glance there were no platform-wide alerts in that timeframe. I'll come back within 4 hours with what we find; if we can't reproduce we'll propose a small compensatory credit and recommended client-side validation steps so you can collect a HAR/pcap if it recurs.

Tessa Morgan
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Brightlane streaming gap — initial triage

Forwarding internal triage notes.

On Wed, Sep 1, 2026 at 09:18 AM Sarah Thompson <sarah@brightlane.com> wrote:
> [original message omitted]

Investigation summary (what I ran):
- Pulled ingress and streamer traces for brl-9f3a2c and surrounding minute (logs attached: redwood-request-logs-20260901.txt).
- Replayed a batch of 5k synthetic streaming requests from our lab that mirror Brightlane's average token length and concurrency. No gaps found.
- Tested against gpt-compat-1 and gpt-compat-2 (same code path). No anomalies seen.

Findings:
- For brl-9f3a2c there is a normal sequence of stream events (open, continuation frames, close). The server-side tokens include the full sentence. There is one short TCP retransmit visible in the network trace from an edge node (approx 1.2s window), but it's followed by correct retransmission and no connection close.
- We could not reproduce the omission at scale. The event looks materially consistent with a client-side buffer/display/SDK stitching issue where a small window of frames is not processed before the final close callback.

Next steps:
- Connor to validate the SDK (Node client) behavior with streamed fragmented frames and confirm whether a race can skip a middle chunk if backpressure triggers an early 'end' handling.
- Tessa to request a HAR or raw stdout from Brightlane if they can reproduce with the curl technique.
- If Brightlane can capture one more occurrence we will correlate a full pcap and provide a deeper TCP-level timeline.

No platform incident to escalate at this point. I recommend we label this as "awaiting customer repro" and offer a 50 USD credit once we close the thread as a goodwill gesture.

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Odd partial gap in streaming response — example attached

Hi Sarah — thanks again for raising this and for the example request id. Quick summary of what we found after triage:

What we checked:
- We inspected server-side streaming traces for the request id you provided and for surrounding traffic. The server produced a complete sequence of streaming frames and closed the connection normally.
- We ran a larger internal replay and could not reproduce the missing middle sentence.
- There is a single, small TCP retransmit recorded in the edge node trace for the time you reported, but the TCP stack completed the retransmit and the application-level stream stayed intact.

Conclusion:
- We do not see evidence of a platform-side drop or truncated stream. Based on the logs, the most likely explanation is a client-side SDK or display race where a short burst of frames was not stitched into the visible buffer before completion. Connor (cc'd) will run a focused SDK test that simulates fragmented frames and backpressure; if a reproduction is found we will share a root cause and fix.

Recommended next steps for Brightlane (if you see this again):
- If possible, run the enclosed curl test to capture the raw stream and attach the raw output or a HAR.
- If you prefer, set DEBUG=redwood:stream on your node process and share stdout.
- Send any additional request_id(s) and exact timestamps so we can correlate at TCP level.

Offer: We appreciate the time you spent helping us validate. Since this was disruptive to your tests we will apply a $50 account credit against your next invoice and keep monitoring. If you would like, we can schedule a short call with Connor to run repro attempts together.

Thanks — please let me know if you'd like that call.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
